transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Well... I suppose I came in because I've just had this feeling lately. It's quiet, but... stubborn. Just this sense that the best version of my life is already behind me. 

I've always been someone who plans things out, stays disciplined, but... it just feels like no amount of that is going to get me back to feeling like myself anymore. So... that's why I'm here.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy most days, especially over the past two weeks?

I suppose so. I mean... I'm not in tears, or anything dramatic like that. It's just... most days, there's this low, gray tone running underneath everything. Even when I'm out in the studio, or... just sitting across from my wife at dinner. It's just sort of there.
Can you recall if there have been times recently when activities you used to enjoy, like being in the studio, didn’t bring you any satisfaction at all?
I don't know about "no satisfaction at all." It's just... different now. I still go out there. I still do the work. It just doesn't feel the same as it used to.
Can you describe if and how the enjoyment you used to get from activities, like being in the studio or spending time with your wife, has changed?
I don't really know how to describe it. It's just... duller, I guess. We still have dinner together. I still work on my projects. It's just... not what it was.
Can you tell me if, most days, you feel like you don’t get any real pleasure or interest from things you used to care about, even a little bit?
I don't think it's... completely gone. I mean, I still care. It's just... muted. That's all.
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed a significant loss of interest in your work in the studio or other activities you used to enjoy, even when you’re doing them?
No, I wouldn't call it a significant loss. I mean... I still do the work. It's just, like I said, a bit muted now. But I haven't stopped doing it.
Can you tell me if, most days, you feel like even small moments of joy or satisfaction from things you used to like are noticeably harder to feel, even a little bit?
No, I wouldn't say that. It's... they aren't harder to feel, really. I still feel them. It's just... I don't know. It's fine.
Can you describe how your mood has been outside of these muted feelings—like, are you generally feeling down or irritable most days, even when things are going okay?

I wouldn't say I'm irritable. It's more... I'm not in tears or anything dramatic like that. It's just... there's this low, gray tone running underneath everything most days. Even when things are fine, like when I'm in the studio, or... just sitting across from my wife at dinner. It's just there.
Can you tell me if, most days, you've been feeling like you're not living up to your own expectations or that you've let yourself or others down in some way?
No, I... I don't think so. I haven't really felt like I'm letting anyone down. I just do what I need to do.
Can you tell me if, most days, you feel like you don’t have the energy to do even the things you used to do without thinking about it?

I mean... I still get up and do things. I do the shopping, tinker with my projects. I'm not just lying around. 

But... I suppose it does take more out of me lately. Just small things, like... setting up for a mentoring session, or walking through a community event. I get worn out. And... taking a nap doesn't really fix it. I just stay tired.
Can you tell me if there have been days when you felt absolutely no pleasure or satisfaction from things you usually care about, even things that used to bring you joy?
I don't think so. I mean, I still enjoy things well enough. I still care about my projects. It's not like I feel nothing at all.
Can you tell me if this low, gray feeling you’ve been having has been present most days for the past two years or more?
I suppose so... yes. It's been going on since I had a hiking injury. That was... a little over three years ago. Maybe three years and three months now, if I had to guess. So, yes.
